reason: Key correct, one answer; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Which kind of speech would make people listen closely and not want it to end?
fields.whyA: Monotonous means dull and in one flat tone; it would bore an audience, not captivate it.
fields.whyC: Vague means unclear; an unclear speech loses listeners instead of holding them.
fields.whyD: Abrupt means sudden or curt; it describes how a speech ends or its tone, not why it captivates.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'eloquent' ay magaling at malinaw magsalita, kaya na-captivate ang audience. Yung ibang choices (monotonous, vague, abrupt) ay negative, kaya hindi sila tugma sa 'captivated'.
fields.hintTl: Anong klaseng speech ang gugustuhin mong pakinggan hanggang dulo?

reason: 'The cat jumped on the table' is also standard; stem now forces 'over' (clearing without touching).

fields.text: Fill in the blank: The horse jumped _____ the fence without touching it.
fields.explanation: 'Over' shows movement from one side of something to the other, passing above it. 'Without touching it' rules out 'on', which means landing on the fence's surface.
fields.hint: The horse never touched the fence. Which preposition means passing above something to the other side?
fields.whyA: 'On' means landing on the surface of the fence, which contradicts 'without touching it'.
fields.whyC: 'In' means inside something; you cannot jump inside a fence.
fields.whyD: 'At' shows direction toward a target (jumped at someone), not clearing an obstacle.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'over' ay paglampas sa ibabaw papunta sa kabilang side. Dahil sabi 'without touching it', hindi pwede ang 'on' kasi ibig sabihin nun lumapag siya sa fence.
fields.hintTl: Hindi tinamaan ng kabayo ang fence. Anong preposition ang ibig sabihin ay lumampas sa ibabaw?

reason: Key correct; 'news' is always singular; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: 'News' ends in -s, but is it really plural?
fields.whyA: 'The' is the correct article here; nothing is wrong with it.
fields.whyB: 'News' is the correct noun; the problem is the verb that agrees with it.
fields.whyD: 'Good' is a correct predicate adjective after a linking verb.
fields.explanationTl: Kahit may -s sa dulo, ang 'news' ay singular (uncountable noun). Kaya dapat 'The news is good', hindi 'are'.
fields.hintTl: May -s ang 'news', pero plural ba talaga siya?

reason: Key correct; set difficulty to 1 (basic preposition); added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Ownership with 'belong' always uses the same preposition: belong ___ someone.
fields.whyB: 'Belong with' means fitting in a group or place (that cup belongs with the set), not ownership.
fields.whyC: 'For' is a common Filipino-English slip; 'belong for' is not standard English.
fields.whyD: 'Of' shows possession in phrases like 'the book of John', but 'belong' does not take 'of'.
fields.explanationTl: Ang tamang idiom ay 'belong to' kapag pagmamay-ari. 'The book belongs to her' = kanya ang libro.
fields.hintTl: Pag ownership, laging 'belong ___ someone'. Anong preposition yun?

reason: 'The team play well' is standard British usage (collective plural); replaced with an unambiguous agreement error.

fields.text: Identify the error: 'Each of the players play well.'
fields.explanation: The subject is 'Each', which is always singular; 'of the players' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'plays'.
fields.hint: Find the real subject first. Is it 'Each' or 'players'?
fields.whyA: 'Each' is correct; it is the singular subject the verb must agree with.
fields.whyB: 'Players' is correctly plural inside the phrase 'of the players'; it is not the subject.
fields.whyD: 'Well' is the correct adverb for the verb 'play'; 'good' would be the mistake.
fields.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'Each', at laging singular yan. Yung 'of the players' ay prepositional phrase lang, hindi siya ang subject. Kaya dapat 'Each of the players plays well.'
fields.hintTl: Hanapin muna ang totoong subject. 'Each' ba o 'players'?

reason: Key correct; 'scissors' is always plural; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Some nouns name one object but are always plural, like 'pants' and 'eyeglasses'.
fields.whyA: 'The' is the correct article; nothing is wrong with it.
fields.whyB: 'Scissors' is the correct form; 'scissor' as a noun for the tool is not standard.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'scissors' ay laging plural, tulad ng 'pants' at 'eyeglasses'. Kaya dapat 'The scissors are sharp.'
fields.hintTl: May mga noun na isang bagay lang pero laging plural, tulad ng 'pants'.

reason: Key correct; set difficulty to 1 (basic tense); added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Look for the helping verb that points to something that has not happened yet.
fields.whyA: 'She eats' is simple present, for habits or general facts.
fields.whyB: 'She ate' is simple past; the action is already done.
fields.whyD: 'She is eating' is present progressive, an action happening right now.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'will + base verb' ay simple future tense. Ang 'will eat' ay kakain pa lang siya.
fields.hintTl: Hanapin ang helping verb na nagsasabing mangyayari pa lang.

reason: 'The jury have decided' is standard British usage; replaced with an unambiguous agreement error.

fields.text: Identify the error: 'Every member of the jury have voted.'
fields.explanation: The subject is 'member', made singular by 'Every'; 'of the jury' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'has voted'.
fields.hint: What is the head noun of the subject, and is it singular or plural?
fields.whyA: 'Every' is correct; it is what makes the subject singular.
fields.whyB: 'Member' is correctly singular after 'Every'; 'members' would be wrong.
fields.whyD: 'Voted' is the correct past participle; only the helping verb is wrong.
fields.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'member', at singular siya dahil sa 'Every'. Yung 'of the jury' ay phrase lang. Kaya dapat 'Every member of the jury has voted.'
fields.hintTl: Ano ang main noun ng subject? Singular ba o plural?

reason: Key correct; one answer; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Ignore 'of the decision'. What is the real subject?
fields.whyA: 'Were' is plural; the subject 'impact' is singular.
fields.whyC: 'Are' is plural and also present tense; the subject 'impact' is singular.
fields.whyD: 'Have significant' is ungrammatical; 'significant' is an adjective and needs a linking verb like 'was'.
fields.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'impact' (singular), hindi 'decision'. Kaya singular verb: 'The impact of the decision was significant.'
fields.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the decision'. Ano ang totoong subject?

reason: Key correct; one answer; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Ignore 'of the experiment'. Is the real subject singular or plural?
fields.whyA: 'Was' agrees with 'experiment', the noun closest to the blank, but the subject is 'results'.
fields.whyC: 'Is' is singular; the subject 'results' is plural.
fields.whyD: 'Has surprising' is ungrammatical; an adjective needs a linking verb, and 'has' is singular anyway.
fields.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'results' (plural), hindi 'experiment'. Kaya plural verb: 'The results of the experiment were surprising.'
fields.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the experiment'. Singular ba o plural ang totoong subject?

reason: Option C 'Beautiful are the flowers' was a valid inversion and capital 'Flowers' misled; replaced C, lowercased the stem.

fields.explanation: A basic English sentence follows article + noun (subject), then the linking verb, then the adjective: 'The flowers are beautiful.'
fields.hint: Start with the subject (article + noun), then the verb.
fields.whyA: It puts the adjective 'beautiful' in the subject slot and the noun after the verb, so the sentence makes no sense.
fields.whyC: The verb 'are' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'flowers'.
fields.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
fields.explanationTl: Ang basic na ayos: article + noun (subject), tapos verb, tapos adjective. Kaya 'The flowers are beautiful.'
fields.hintTl: Unahin ang subject (article + noun), saka ang verb.

reason: Option C 'Sleeping is the cat' is an arguable inversion and capital 'Cat' misled; replaced C, lowercased the stem, fixed 'gerund' (it is a present participle).

fields.explanation: The subject 'the cat' comes first, then the progressive verb 'is sleeping' (helping verb + present participle): 'The cat is sleeping.'
fields.hint: Keep the article with its noun, and keep 'is' right before 'sleeping'.
fields.whyA: It puts 'sleeping' in the subject slot and leaves 'cat' at the end with no role.
fields.whyC: The verb 'is' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'cat'.
fields.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
fields.explanationTl: Una ang subject na 'the cat', tapos ang verb na 'is sleeping' (helping verb + -ing). Kaya 'The cat is sleeping.'
fields.hintTl: Dapat magkasama ang article at noun, at 'is' bago ang 'sleeping'.

reason: Stem was awkward, 'No implication' was a junk option and B was loosely worded; tightened B and D, same key.

fields.text: What is implied by the sentence 'The movie was exciting, but the ending was predictable.'?
fields.optionB: The ending was less exciting than the rest of the movie.
fields.explanation: 'But' sets up a contrast: the movie overall was exciting, while the ending, being predictable, did not keep up that excitement.
fields.hint: What does the word 'but' contrast the ending with?
fields.whyA: Too strong: the sentence calls the movie exciting, so it does not say the movie was bad.
fields.whyC: Contradicts the sentence: a predictable ending is the opposite of a surprising one.
fields.whyD: Overgeneralizes: only the ending is called predictable; the rest was exciting.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'but' ay nagpapakita ng contrast: exciting ang movie, pero predictable ang ending, kaya hindi kasing-exciting ang ending kumpara sa iba.
fields.hintTl: Ano ang kinokontra ng 'but' sa ending?

reason: Key correct; distractors are all antonyms, no second synonym; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: A businessman described this way would be hard to fool.
fields.whyA: Foolish is the opposite of astute.
fields.whyC: Naive means inexperienced and easily fooled, the opposite of astute.
fields.whyD: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, the opposite of astute.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'astute' ay matalino at magaling bumasa ng sitwasyon, parang 'shrewd' o wais. Ang ibang choices ay kabaligtaran.
fields.hintTl: Ang ganitong businessman ay mahirap lokohin.

reason: Key correct; one synonym; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: Think of a long climb up a steep mountain.
fields.whyA: Easy is the opposite of arduous.
fields.whyC: Simple is the opposite of arduous.
fields.whyD: Effortless is the opposite of arduous, which means needing great effort.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'arduous' ay mahirap at nakakapagod, kailangan ng matinding effort. Kaya 'difficult' ang sagot.
fields.hintTl: Isipin ang pag-akyat sa matarik na bundok.

reason: Key correct; one synonym; added teaching fields.

fields.hint: How would you feel facing this task before you even start?
fields.whyA: Easy is the opposite; a daunting task looks hard.
fields.whyC: Simple is the opposite; a daunting task looks complicated.
fields.whyD: Straightforward is the opposite; a daunting task looks overwhelming.
fields.explanationTl: Ang 'daunting' ay nakakatakot o nakakapanghina ng loob dahil mukhang mahirap. Kaya 'intimidating' ang sagot.
fields.hintTl: Ano ang pakiramdam mo bago mo pa simulan ang ganitong task?

reason: Banned 'Both A and B' / 'None' option set; rewritten as an in-context meaning item on the same word.

fields.text:
The scientist examined the minute details of the cell.

In this sentence, 'minute' most nearly means:
fields.explanation: As an adjective (pronounced my-NOOT), 'minute' means extremely small; details of a cell are tiny. The time-unit meaning (MIN-it) is a noun and does not fit here.
fields.hint: Here 'minute' describes details. How big are the details of a single cell?
fields.whyB: That is the noun 'minute' (60 seconds); in this sentence the word is an adjective describing 'details'.
fields.whyC: Confuses 'minute' with doing something 'in a minute' (quickly); the word describes size, not speed.
fields.whyD: Details can be important, but 'minute' describes their size, not their importance.
fields.explanationTl: Dito, adjective ang 'minute' (basa: my-NOOT) at ang ibig sabihin ay napakaliit. Ang 'minute' na 60 seconds ay noun, kaya hindi bagay dito.
fields.hintTl: Inilalarawan ng 'minute' ang details. Gaano kalaki ang details ng isang cell?
